headline: GERMANY STRIKES IN THE WEST
body: German forces crossed into Holland, Belgium and Luxembourg at dawn. The long-expected offensive has begun.

headline: THE DUNKIRK EVACUATION BEGINS
body: Operation Dynamo is under way. The Navy and a fleet of little ships are lifting the Army off the beaches under constant air attack.

headline: DUNKIRK: THE LAST MEN COME HOME
body: The evacuation is complete. Over 300,000 men have been brought back across the Channel. Fighter Command covered the beaches at heavy cost.

headline: 'THEIR FINEST HOUR'
body: The Prime Minister has told the Commons that the Battle of France is over and the Battle of Britain is about to begin.

headline: THE CHANNEL BATTLE OPENS
body: The Luftwaffe has begun sustained attacks on Channel convoys and the coastal towns. Every raid is being met.

headline: ADLERTAG: THE GREAT ASSAULT
body: The enemy threw his full weight against the airfields of southern England in what he calls 'Eagle Day'. The attacks were broken up.

headline: THE HARDEST FIGHTING YET
body: The Luftwaffe mounted its largest effort of the war, striking from Northumberland to Kent. Losses on both sides were severe.

headline: THE HARDEST DAY
body: Waves of bombers came for the sector stations. Kenley and Biggin Hill were hit. The defenders held.

headline: 'NEVER WAS SO MUCH OWED'
body: The Prime Minister paid tribute to the fighter pilots: never in the field of human conflict was so much owed by so many to so few.

headline: BOMBS FALL ON LONDON
body: For the first time bombs have fallen on the capital. A reply against Berlin is expected.

headline: FIGHTER COMMAND'S COSTLIEST DAY
body: The sector airfields took a heavy battering. Ground crews worked through the night to keep the squadrons flying.

headline: THE ENEMY TURNS ON LONDON
body: In a great daylight raid the Luftwaffe struck the London docks. The airfields have a respite; the city has not.

headline: 92 SQUADRON TO BIGGIN HILL
body: No. 92 Squadron has moved south to Biggin Hill and into the thick of the fighting in 11 Group.

headline: THE GREATEST DAY
body: Two massive daylight assaults on London were met and turned back with heavy enemy losses.

headline: DAYLIGHT RAIDS REPULSED
body: Large formations crossing Kent were broken up before they reached London. The enemy's daylight effort is faltering.

headline: THE ENEMY CHANGES HIS METHOD
body: High-flying fighter-bomber sweeps are replacing the mass raids. The squadrons are scrambled to great heights.

headline: INVASION POSTPONED
body: There are signs the enemy has put off his invasion. The pressure in the air has not eased.

headline: THE BATTLE IS WON
body: After sixteen weeks the great daylight assault has been beaten off. Fighter Command holds the sky over Britain.
